content:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + upstream timeouts observed for customer LumosHealth on dedicated-us-west-2-3. Error rate spike started ~10:14 UTC. Current 5xx = 18%, timeouts = 12%. Auto-mitigation not yet triggered. Paging on-call.

sara-oncall: ack — I'm on it, pulling logs now. assigning P1 and starting incident doc. @maria-sre you'll probably want eyes on the pool.

maria-sre: on my way. can someone paste the last 10m of gateway metrics?

kenji-eng: grabbed a quick snapshot from graphite -> gateway_queue_len jumped from 20 -> 420 in ~3m for dedicated-us-west-2-3. KV eviction rate also up.

jordan-se: customer impact: LumosHealth reports ~30% of inference requests failing with 5xx and about half of those are upstream timeouts. Tagging support to assemble recent error samples.

ethan-support: here are the last two sample request IDs from the customer: req_98f4a and req_98f4b. Both show gateway 504 in logs. They confirm major degradation in their production traffic.

maria-sre: running quick health checks on the nodes.
```bash
# check pod status
kubectl -n redwood-dedicated get pods -l pool=dedicated-us-west-2-3 -o wide
# tail gateway logs for 504s
kubectl -n redwood-dedicated logs svc/gateway -c gateway --since=15m | grep "504"
```

kenji-eng: GPUs look saturated on two nodes: nv1-12 and nv1-14. CUDA mem pressure high. Also seeing lots of KV cache misses for LumosHealth prefix — suggests cold cache due to eviction.

sara-oncall: interesting — could be noisy neighbor causing KV pressure + GPU saturation. Options: 1) throttle LumosHealth to reduce qps 2) reroute some of their traffic to fallback model variant (lower mem) 3) add burst capacity (spin up extra nodes) 4) evict suspected noisy tenant. Thoughts?

jordan-se: customer preference: minimal functional change, but they accept temporary fallback to a smaller model if it reduces errors. They do NOT want degraded quality without notice. Coordinate with them?

maria-sre: immediate mitigation plan: scale pool + enable fallback routing for LumosHealth. I'll trigger scale and open canary for fallback model. Also start KV cache warming for LumosHealth keys.

opsbot: Action: scale_pool called by maria-sre on dedicated-us-west-2-3: +3 nodes requested. Provisioning started (req id scale-2365). Estimated ready: 4m.

kenji-eng: meanwhile I can flip routing rule to route 20% of LumosHealth traffic to model-quantized-v1. That should reduce memory pressure. Will monitor for regressions.

sara-oncall: do it but only 20% to start. Add a header for observability: X-Reroute:quantized-test. Also add rate limit of 60rps for their highest-QPS key to buy breathing room.

jordan-se: I've notified LumosHealth support contact: "we're mitigating via partial fallback and capacity scale; you may see some requests routed to a lower-memory model temporarily. We'll confirm quality and revert when stable." They asked for ETA.

maria-sre: scale nodes are up. Verifying pool health. KV eviction rate trending down after warming. Gateway queue length dropping from 420 -> 80.

incident-bot: NOTE: scale_pool complete (scale-2365). New nodes: nv1-21, nv1-22, nv1-23.

kenji-eng: toggled routing: 20% now to model-quantized-v1. Observability tag in place. Initial error rate dropping to 9% 5xx and timeouts at 4%. Still above baseline but trending down. :thumbsup:

ethan-support: LumosHealth confirms their telemetry is improving, fewer end-user errors. They're asking when we can fully shift back.

sara-oncall: hold for 30m of stable 5xx < 2% and timeouts < 1% before rolling back. Maria, keep watch on KV miss rate and GPU util. Kenji, prepare rollback plan for the 20% reroute.

maria-sre: logs show one suspect tenant in same pool spiking burst requests at a pattern that lines up with evictions — likely noisy neighbor. We should throttle that tenant and ask their engineering team to investigate. I'll mark them for follow-up.

jordan-se: opened follow-up ticket to tenant Team "HelioMetrics" for noisy behavior: TICKET-4582. Assigned to platform-eng.

opsbot: Incident doc created: https://incidents.internal/redwood/INC-2026-2365019876 (visibility: eng/sre/ops). Priority: P1.

sara-oncall: summary so far: root cause candidate = noisy tenant causing KV evictions + GPU saturation leading to gateway queue pressure -> elevated 5xx/timeouts. Mitigations: scale + partial fallback routing + KV warming. Current state: stabilizing; 5xx down to 6%. Customer LumosHealth impacted; support notified.

ethan-support: adding customer impact details to incident doc: ~30min outage window, degraded for ~10-15% of users, no data loss. Customer wants a postmortem and follow-up on noisy tenant.

kenji-eng: preparing postmitigation tasks: 1) enforce per-tenant QPS caps on the pool 2) improve KV eviction priority for pinned prefixes 3) add automatic fallback rule when queue_len > 200.

maria-sre: agreed. Also will add an alert for sudden kv_eviction_rate spikes per pool.

sara-oncall: handing off to night oncall @maria-sre in 45m. I'll leave the incident open and update status in the doc. Please escalate if error rate goes back above 10% or customer reports new regressions.

jordan-se: tagging postmortem owner: @kenji-eng. ETA for draft: EOD tomorrow.

incident-bot: RESOLVE_CHECK: current 5xx = 3%, timeouts = 1.2%. Will auto-close if stable for 45m.

sara-oncall: closing comments before handoff: good job team. Keep the follow-ups (tenant throttle + permanent QPS cap + better fallback triggers). Handing to maria for overnight watch. :heart:

maria-sre: taking over. I'll post an update in the morning and coordinate with platform-eng to throttle the noisy tenant.

ethan-support: I'll send a concise customer update with mitigation steps and promise of a postmortem.

jordan-se: thanks all.

incident-bot: Thread moved to status: monitoring."
